title: Cap. III Sol. Rat. 14: adversaries conflate antecedents of glory with antecedents of God's intention
pass_a_gloss: But in this the adversaries slip, that they think those things which are antecedents to eternal life, to which men are elected, must also necessarily be conceived as antecedents to the act or intention of the one electing, that is, to God's decree by which they are elected. For that internal and eternal act of the Divine will by which he elects, and glory, or heavenly joy, to which he elects, are greatly diverse. Whence we can rightly affirm something of the object which we cannot affirm except falsely of the act or intention of God by which that object is destined to a singular person. For example: This assertion about the object is true: Paul's calling, justification, and pious life or working are seen by God as preceding his glorification: but the same is false if it is fitted to God's act in this manner: Paul's calling, and justification, and pious life or working are seen by God as preceding the Divine intention concerning glorifying Paul.
pass_b_english: Here the adversaries slip: they think what precedes eternal life (to which men are elected) must also be conceived as preceding the elector's act or intention — God's decree by which they are elected. But that internal eternal act of the divine will by which he elects, and the glory or heavenly joy to which he elects, are greatly different. So we can rightly affirm of the object what we can only falsely affirm of God's act or intention destinating that object to a particular person. Example — true of the object: Paul's calling, justification, and pious life are seen by God as preceding his glorification. False if fitted to God's act: those same are seen by God as preceding the divine intention to glorify Paul.
source_text: Sed in hoc labuntur adversarii, quod arbitrantur ea quae sunt antecedentia ad vitam aeternam, ad quam homines eliguntur, concipi etiam necessario oportere ut antecedentia ad actum sive intentionem eligentis, id est, Dei decretum, a quo eliguntur. Nam actus ille internus et aeternus voluntatis Divinae, quo eligit, et gloria, sive caeleste gaudium, ad quod eligit, sunt valde diversa. Unde possumus aliquid recte affirmare de objecto, quod non possumus nisi falso affirmare de actu sive intentione Dei qua illud objectum singulari personae destinatur. Verbi causa; Vera est haec assertio de objecto: Vocatio Pauli, justificatio, et pia vita sive operatio videntur a Deo ut praecedanea ad ejus glorificationem: sed falsa est eadem si ad actum Dei accommodetur, hoc modo, Vocatio Pauli, et justificatio, et pia vita sive operatio videntur a Deo ut praecedanea ad intentionem Divinam de Paulo glorificando.
